answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable bond before earning rewards, then slash bonds tied to coordinated fraud. Rewards grow with a bond’s age, so an attacker must lock real capital in every fake account and wait to build credibility. A new identity may enter through an inlet, but multiplying influence is costly and slow; catching one linked account can send a ripple through the swarm, while even an honest comet of new users faces the same bond rule.
